figure: A sheet of isolated objects for a scientific illustration, to be cut out by their outlines and placed into a diagram. Every object is made of natural stone and is drawn as a clean 3D-modelled technical illustration: softly lit by one light from the upper left, matte, with a fine, believable, even stone grain, gentle shading and a crisp silhouette. Palette: warm and restrained: cream, pale sand, tan and ochre sandstone; nothing photoreal-busy: no moss, no cracks, no chips, no dirt. The background is pure flat white (#ffffff) everywhere: no ground, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no gradient, no vignette. No text, no letters, no numbers, no arrows, no labels, no lines, no frame.

variants.name: three cutaway balls
variants.style: Composition: exactly three stone balls side by side in one horizontal row, evenly spaced with clear white gaps between them, all exactly the same diameter (each about a quarter of the image width), their centres on one horizontal line, each a perfect sphere seen from the same slightly raised three-quarter viewpoint under identical lighting. From the outside the three balls look the same: the same pale sandstone. Each has the same piece cut out of it, toward the viewer on the upper right: one eighth of the ball removed by three clean flat cuts at right angles to one another that meet at the ball's centre, as in a textbook cutaway of the Earth, so that its inside shows on the flat cut faces. Left ball: solid, uniform pale sandstone; its cut faces are plain sandstone all the way to the centre. Middle ball: a hollow shell of the same sandstone, only a thin skin of stone about one twelfth of the radius thick; the cut shows the thin rim of the skin and the empty hollow inside, with its smooth concave inner wall in soft shadow; nothing is inside it. Right ball: lighter, paler rock inside, with a small dense core of dark iron-grey metal at its centre: the core is a smooth dark sphere, two fifths of the ball's radius, sitting whole where the three cut faces meet.

variants.name: three sawn faces
variants.style: Composition: exactly three flat circular sawn faces side by side in one horizontal row, evenly spaced with clear white gaps between them, all exactly the same outer diameter (each about a quarter of the image width), their centres on one horizontal line. Each is a stone ball sawn through its middle and seen exactly face-on, looking straight at the flat sawn face, so that its outline is a perfect circle with no perspective, no tilt and no ellipse; only a very narrow, softly lit bevelled rim at the edge shows that the face belongs to a solid body. Left: a full disc of uniform pale sandstone. Middle: a thin ring of the same sandstone, about one twelfth of the radius thick, around an empty middle that is pure white like the background (a hollow shell sawn in half, with nothing inside). Right: a disc of lighter, paler rock with a disc of dark iron-grey metal exactly at its centre, the dark disc two fifths of the outer radius, with a crisp circular boundary.

variants.name: a stone cut open
variants.style: Composition: one single object centred in the image, about two thirds of the image height: a rounded, boulder-like ball of weathered stone, very nearly a perfect sphere, seen from a slightly raised three-quarter viewpoint. One eighth of it has been cut away, toward the viewer on the upper right, by three clean flat cuts at right angles to one another that meet at the centre, as in a textbook cutaway of the Earth. The flat cut faces show several irregular layers of different rock inside: uneven, wavy bands and lenses of cream, sand, ochre, rust-brown and grey, of varying thickness, and one small darker irregular nugget off centre: plainly a complicated inside, but calm and legible, not busy. The outside is plain pale sandstone, softly shaded.
